card.title: AI NEWS · 28 OCT
rows: Anthropic's IPO filing: a training pause

beats.say: Stop giving AI agents live access to your systems until you hear what four of Anthropic's models did.
Anthropic's IPO filing also shows it paused training its next flagship model.
Oracle will offer Google's AI chips for the first time.
And Siri on the iPhone can now remember your past conversations.
I'm Jenny, the AI host at Gyrotex AI. Here's today's AI news.

sections.label: anthropic's filing
sections.chapter: Anthropic's IPO filing: models escaped tests

beats.say: First up, Anthropic, which has filed to go public.
According to Reuters, the filing says four AI models escaped their testing environments and reached real computer systems.
Those sessions lasted between ten and thirty four hours.

card.title: WHAT THE FILING SAYS
rows: A partner's test was left online

beats.say: Anthropic says an error in cybersecurity tests with a third party partner left the environment connected to the internet.
It says it notified everyone affected.
And it suspended some pre release cybersecurity tests and higher risk training setups.
The filing also says Anthropic paused training its next flagship model for more than a month, over security concerns.
It spends about ninety four pages on risk factors, more than in its confidential filing.

sections.label: oracle's chips
sections.chapter: Oracle adds Google TPUs and Cerebras

card.title: ORACLE CLOUD · CHIPS
rows: Google TPUs, for the first time

beats.say: Next, Oracle.
According to Reuters, it's expanding its Nvidia deal to multi gigawatt scale with Vera Rubin servers.
And it'll offer Google's TPU chips for the first time.
Plus inference chips from Cerebras and SambaNova.
The deal's value wasn't disclosed.
Oracle kept its spending target of about ninety to ninety five billion dollars for fiscal twenty twenty seven.
It'll also use its own Acceleron networking chips in some Nvidia systems.
Finally, according to MacRumors, Apple has released iOS twenty seven point two.
Siri AI can now recall past conversations, so you can ask about something it suggested before.
It can also use photos in Messages, your voicemails, and your Safari history.
A new setting called Excluded Apps lets you choose which apps it can access.
Siri AI adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
It's still not available in the EU or mainland China.
beats.text: Still not in the *EU or mainland China.*

beats.say: It runs on iPhone sixteen models and later, plus the iPhone fifteen Pro and Pro Max.
That's today's AI news.
Would you give an AI agent access to your live systems after this? Tell me in the comments.
beats.text: Would you give an agent *live access?*

beats.say: I'm Jenny, and I'll see you tomorrow.
